pr.title: [mir-opt] simplify `Repeat`s that don't actually repeat the operand
pr.description:
Created because when I was writing this case in GVN

https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/133324/files#diff-292b215fdc6b59e3f3c4173c2270b14591c5673832fbfb05cd69a05c2ef0c30eR977-R979

I happened to notice that it worked for `[x]` but not for `[x; 1]`, so figured it would be good to simplify that `Repeat` to the simpler `Aggregate`.
pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason: The PR is a semantics-preserving MIR optimization/refactor, not a confirmed miscompile. InstSimplify's new `simplify_repeat_once` rewrites `[x; 1]` to `[x]`, which is value-equivalent, while the historical code merely left it as `[x; 1]` (a missed optimization). RemoveZsts' `trivially_zst` refinement likewise only changes when a definitely-ZST type is recognized; the old `maybe_zst` + `layout_of` path still preserved program semantics and did not misclassify the union or scalar cases. Thus there is no source-grounded historical wrong transformation that produces a different observable value on concrete inputs. Encoding one would require fabricating an unrelated semantic bug, which the instructions prohibit.

analysis.summary: This merged mir-opt PR adds InstSimplify's `simplify_repeat_once`, rewriting `Rvalue::Repeat(operand, 1)` into a one-element `Rvalue::Aggregate` `[operand]`, including when the count is a const expression that evaluates to 1. It also refines RemoveZsts' cheap ZST pre-check from `maybe_zst` to `trivially_zst`, which classifies zero-length arrays `[T; 0]` as definitely ZST without `layout_of`, while keeping non-ZST scalars and unions correct. These are missed-optimization/refactor changes, not confirmed miscompiles; no compiler was executed here.
analysis.originalLogic: InstSimplify previously ran `simplify_ptr_aggregate`, `simplify_cast`, and `simplify_repeated_aggregate` for rvalues but had no repeat-once simplifier, so `_2 = [move _3; 1]` and `_0 = [move _4; 1]` remained as `Rvalue::Repeat` rather than becoming the simpler one-element aggregate. RemoveZsts previously used `maybe_zst`: `Adt`, `Array`, `Closure`, `CoroutineClosure`, `Tuple`, and `Alias(Opaque)` returned true as "maybe ZST", `FnDef`/`Never` returned true, and everything else returned false; `known_to_be_zst` then called `layout_of` for the maybe cases. That could miss `[T; 0]` with generic `T` when `layout_of` was not usable.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historically, for InstSimplify the transformation was the identity on a repeat count of 1: `[move _3; 1]` stayed `[move _3; 1]` instead of becoming `[move _3]`. This was a missed simplification, not a wrong rewrite. For RemoveZsts, the historical `known_to_be_zst` could return false for a generic zero-length array like `[T; 0]` because it depended on `layout_of`; consequently the zero-sized local was not replaced with `const ZeroSized: [T; 0]`. The pre-PR code did not incorrectly mark unions or scalars as ZST: the union test still produced `_0 = Foo { x: const () };`.
analysis.inputDomain: InstSimplify input domain: MIR assignments whose rvalue is `Rvalue::Repeat(operand, count)` where `count.try_to_target_usize(tcx)` yields exactly `Some(1)`. The count may be a literal `1` or a const expression that evaluates to 1, as in the test's `const MYSTERY: usize = 3_usize.pow(2) - 2_usize.pow(3);`. Operands can be moved or copied values of generic type `T`; the test uses `T: Copy`. RemoveZsts input domain: types passed through its ZST check, especially `ty::Array(_ty, len)` where `len.try_to_target_usize(tcx) == Some(0)`, including generic element types; also union ADTs and scalar types that must not be misclassified.
analysis.trigger: InstSimplify: an rvalue matching `Rvalue::Repeat(operand, count)` with `let Some(1) = count.try_to_target_usize(self.tcx)`. RemoveZsts: `trivially_zst(ty, tcx)` returning `Some(true)`, notably for `ty::Array(_ty, len)` with `Some(0) = len.try_to_target_usize(tcx)`; if it returns `None`, the pass still falls back to `layout_of`.
preconditions: InstSimplify must be processing an assignment/rvalue in its rvalue-simplification path, after the existing `simplify_ptr_aggregate`, `simplify_cast`, and `simplify_repeated_aggregate` calls.
The repeat count must successfully evaluate to target-usize 1; `try_to_target_usize` returning `None` or any other value must not trigger the rewrite.
The replacement aggregate kind is `AggregateKind::Array(operand.ty(self.local_decls, self.tcx))` and contains exactly the original operand once.
RemoveZsts' `trivially_zst` must return `Some(true)` only for definitely-ZST types; `Some(false)` for definitely non-ZST scalars; and `None` for types that still need `layout_of`.
A zero-length array is definitely ZST only when its length evaluates to exactly 0; unions such as `Foo { x: (), y: u64 }` are not ZST just because one field is zero-sized.
pitfalls: Do not rewrite `[x; N]` for N other than exactly 1, including N = 0 or N > 1; only the one-element case becomes `[x]`.
Do not test only literal `1`: the count may be a const expression, and the regression test deliberately uses `MYSTERY = 3^2 - 2^3 = 1` to exercise `try_to_target_usize`.
Preserve the operand exactly once in the new aggregate; for count 1 there must be no duplication, and move/copy semantics of the original operand should be retained.
For RemoveZsts, don't assume `[T; 0]` can be recognized via `layout_of` for generic `T`; the syntactic zero-length check is what makes the generic case removable.
Do not classify all ADTs as ZST. The union `Foo { x: (), y: u64 }` is not ZST, and the updated test checks `_0 = Foo { x: const () };` rather than a ZeroSized constant.
After RemoveZsts replaces a local, expect `StorageLive`, the assignment, and `StorageDead` to become `nop`, and debug info to refer to `const ZeroSized: [T; 0]`; the actual storage is gone.
The two changes are independent: a program can exercise InstSimplify repeat-one simplification without exercising RemoveZsts zero-length-array removal, and vice versa.
analysis.testStrategy: Use focused MIR-opt tests tagged with the exact pass. For InstSimplify, use `//@ test-mir-pass: InstSimplify-after-simplifycfg`, `//@ compile-flags: -C panic=abort`, and `#![crate_type = "lib"]`; define `pub fn repeat_once_to_aggregate<T: Copy>(x: T) -> [T; 1]` containing both `let other = [x; MYSTERY];` with `MYSTERY` evaluating to 1 and a literal `[x; 1]`. Check that no `[move _; 1]` remains and that assignments are `[move _]`. For RemoveZsts, use `//@ test-mir-pass: RemoveZsts`; test generic `fn remove_generic_array<T: Copy>(x: T)` with `let a = [x; 0];` and `let b = [x; MYSTERY];` where `MYSTERY = 280_usize.isqrt() - 260_usize.isqrt() = 0`; check debug locals become `const ZeroSized: [T; 0]` and no `= []` remains. Also test a union with a zero-sized field and a non-ZST field, checking it remains `Foo { x: const () };` and is not treated as ZeroSized.
evidence: `Some(true)` is definitely ZST; `Some(false)` is definitely *not* ZST.
ty::Array(_ty, len) if let Some(0) = len.try_to_target_usize(tcx) => Some(true),
`None` may or may not be, and must check `layout_of` to be sure.
